edge_board.description: Heightened tensions from the ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict, including renewed military activity in July 2026, continue to shape trader assessments of potential Israeli airspace closures. Israeli authorities have closed and reopened the Tel Aviv FIR multiple times earlier in 2026 amid Iranian missile and drone responses to strikes. As of early August, civil aviation remains operational with Ben-Gurion Airport functioning normally, though EASA maintains advisories on elevated risks and the US Embassy issued an August 1 alert citing possible short-notice disruptions. Diplomats and military statements are closely watched for signs of escalation that could trigger temporary restrictions before key deadlines.
edge_board.question: Israel closes its airspace by August 15?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Will any company announce that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) before Oct 1, 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria: If any company (public or private) officially announces that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) after market issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes. To qualify, the announcement must explicitly state that the company has achieved, attained, reached, or developed Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), or that it has achieved, attained, reached, or developed “AGI.” Statements that describe “AGI-like,” “AGI-level,” “near-AGI,” or “toward AGI” systems without explicitly stating that the company has achieved/attained/reached/developed AGI do not qualify. For purposes of this market, a “company” includes any publicly traded company or any privately held company whose existence and corporate identity is verifiable and whose financing/valuation or corporate profile is covered by at least two of the listed major business news sources.

edge_board.description: **No change leads at 62.5%** because the FOMC held rates at the 3.5–3.75% range in its July 29 decision by a 9-3 vote amid elevated inflation and solid labor conditions, with the majority preferring to await fresh July and August CPI and employment data before the mid-September meeting. Persistent core PCE inflation near 3.3% and headline pressures from recent oil-price spikes tied to Middle East tensions have kept hawkish concerns alive, supporting the 34.5% odds on a 25-basis-point hike. Markets assign negligible probability to cuts because employment remains near maximum-employment levels and inflation has not yet returned to the 2% target. The September outcome will hinge on whether incoming inflation prints show sustained energy-driven upside or begin to moderate.
edge_board.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

edge_board.description: Ongoing geopolitical tensions from the U.S.-Iran conflict have kept daily transits through the Strait of Hormuz at 9–16 vessels recently versus the pre-2026 average of 60–100, severely constraining flows that account for roughly 20–25% of global seaborne crude and significant LNG volumes. This has supported elevated energy prices and prompted rerouting costs while traders monitor Iran-Oman negotiations over a safe shipping corridor announced in early August. Recent AIS data show only marginal improvement despite earlier cease-fire signals, with insurance premiums and security risks continuing to limit tanker participation. Key near-term catalysts include further diplomatic progress and any verifiable uptick in PortWatch-measured arrivals that could shift market-implied odds on normalization timelines.
edge_board.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by August 31?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and August 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for August 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

edge_board.question: Will Davante Adams announce his retirement before the 2026-27 NFL season?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
If Davante Adams announces his retirement from the NFL before the 2026-27 NFL season start date, then the market resolves to Yes. Note: The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to the first new season after the announcement.

For the purposes of this market, the NFL season start date is defined as the date of the first regular season game for that season.
